correctness.rationale: The group is exponent 2, so Hermitian positive-definite Fourier coefficients a_e are real and positivity is precisely 1+Σ_e a_e s_u s_v>=0 for every sign vector. Writing W=Σ_e a_e gives a(C)<= (1+W)/2 for every graph cut C. Averaging those inequalities over the edge-transitive orbit of a maximum cut yields (M/m)W<=(1+W)/2; strict M>m/2 follows because a random cut has mean m/2 and the empty cut has zero. Therefore 1+W<=2M/(2M-m). The uniform coefficient c=1/(2M-m) gives Fourier values 1+c(m-2|C|)>=0 and attains the bound. For an odd cycle each maximum cut is the complement of a single edge: equality for all such cuts forces W-a_e=(1+W)/2 and hence every a_e=1/(2k-1), proving uniqueness. Independently enumerated all cuts and Fourier values for C5, K4, K5 and Petersen, confirming e.g. 8/3, 4, 6, 8/3; these finite checks are not the infinite edge-transitive proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The earlier sharp weight-two Hamming shell theorem specializes to complete-graph supports and does not cover all edge-transitive H. Šámal’s x(H) = |E|/M and χ_q=2/(2-x) already determine the numerical cubical chromatic value; the extra unaddressed statement identifies it with a Fourier-positive extremum and proves its extremizer. Blow-up invariance covers specific multipartite graph families but not arbitrary edge-transitive graph shells.

originality.rationale: The new mathematical statement is the explicit bridge from positive-definite finite-group Turán mass to cut covering and cubical coloring, with the exact Fourier extremizer and uniqueness for odd cycles. Šámal proves the cut-cover LP and its edge-transitive x=m/M equality, and the earlier Boolean Hamming-shell calculation gives K_n as a special case; none of the inspected originals states the Boolean-edge-shell positive-definite identity for arbitrary edge-transitive graphs or its normalized odd-cycle rigidity. This judgment credits the existing graph parameter formulas rather than treating an algebraic relabeling as all-new.
residual_risks: A differently named positive-type Cayley kernel/cut-polytope identity may predate the bridge; targeted public indexing cannot prove absolute priority.
No classification of all extremizers for every edge-transitive graph and no general non-edge-transitive sharp formula.

value.rationale: The Boolean shell of graph edge-incidence vectors is a natural family of spectral supports. The equality transfers MAXCUT values into exact harmonic positive-type masses for all finite edge-transitive graphs, unifies complete graphs, odd cycles and Petersen by a structural argument, and classifies odd-cycle positive-definite optimizers; it is more than a new notation for a single precomputed constant.

final_claim: For a nonempty finite simple edge-transitive H, the positive-definite Turán mass of its Boolean edge shell is 2 MAXCUT(H)/(2 MAXCUT(H)-|E|), equal to the cubical chromatic number; the given uniform coefficients attain equality; odd cycles have unique normalized optimizer.
